projects.title: CivSwitch
projects.summary: Civilization VII userland entry point, with Pico 1 and Pico 2 firmware.
projects.requirements: Physical Switch 1 edition cartridge, game version 1.0.0, compatible RP2040/RP2350 Pico. Author lists firmware 20.x–23.0.1 and reports Switch 2 tests on 20.4.0 and 23.0.1.
projects.setup: Follow PicoSwitch’s instructions using the UF2 for your Pico model. The wireless multiplayer lobby chat starts the remote JavaScript loader on port 9026. The optional persistent save-trigger installer wipes save:/saves/Single/; back up your Civilization VII saves first. UF2 files are Pico firmware, not Switch app packages.
projects.status: 1.0 · ready Pico firmware; installer and host scripts remain in the project.

projects.title: ns2jb
projects.summary: pepsipu’s Switch 2 execution research and FS demo.
projects.requirements: Demo: firmware 23.0.1, SmileBASIC 4.4.9, Node.js 22+ on macOS/Linux, over 20 MiB free in the SmileBASIC save and a reachable LAN connection.
projects.setup: Prepare bootstrap.bas and the computer-side run.cjs host using the upstream README. Keep SmileBASIC open during the demo; restart the console afterwards. This demo installs no CFW or persistence. Savekit and OunceCake need their own documented RPC engine/fork; the plain FS demo is not a substitute.
projects.status: Original and RPC upstream ZIP links available. Local copies are pending: GitLab archive requests returned406, then its IP rate limit returned429 until2November2026,10:00UTC. No incomplete package is offered as a local download.
guideSteps: Extract the chosen package

Keep the complete extracted folder together. Use the original package for the standalone demo; use the separately labelled RPC fork for Savekit or OunceCake. Install Node.js22+ on the documented macOS/Linux host.
Prepare SmileBASIC
Use firmware23.0.1 and SmileBASIC4.4.9 for the original demo. Enter the included bootstrap.bas in slot0 and save it as NS2. Keep more than20MiB free in the application save.
Start the host

In the original extracted folder run node run.cjs <computer-LAN-IP>. For dependent tools, use the RPC folder and node run.cjs --rpc <computer-LAN-IP>. Follow that fork’s Ethernet and internal-storage requirements.
Pair and keep the session open
Follow the included README’s Direct-mode sequence and the exact V=START line printed by the host. Keep SmileBASIC and the host open. Use the printed runs/switch2-* folder for dependent tools.
Finish or recover
Finish all dependent operations before stopping the host with Ctrl+C. Restart the console after a failed or uncertain session. Preserve run logs for diagnosis.

projects.title: ns2-savekit
projects.summary: Back up, verify, restore and modify title saves through ns2jb. Includes separate Artemis Lua save-launch tools.
projects.requirements: Patched ns2jb RPC engine, live session and run folder/current-root.json, Node.js, firmware 23.0.1 and retail SmileBASIC 4.
projects.setup: Apply the documented engine patches before starting a fresh RPC session. Open tools/kit.cjs with the run folder. Begin with read-only listing and backup, then verify by hash. Keep originals before restore/replace/delete operations. No npm install or compilation is required by the author; this project does not include the exploit, keys or games.
projects.status: Pinned complete script/source ZIP with tools, patches, configuration and upstream documentation. Requires the separate RPC download.
guideSteps: Extract both downloads separately
Keep Savekit and the RPC fork in separate folders. Retain every engine, tools, patches and config directory; do not run kit.cjs alone.
Prepare the required engine patches

The upstream patch command expects a Git working tree. For an extracted RPC ZIP, run git init inside that RPC folder first. From Savekit, follow sh patches/apply.sh /absolute/path/to/ns2jb-rpc. If any patch fails, stop and resolve the revision mismatch before starting a session.
Start a fresh RPC session
Use the RPC setup above, with node run.cjs --rpc <computer-LAN-IP>, and keep it running. A run folder from before patching retains the old engine and must not be reused.
Open the kit

From the extracted Savekit folder run node tools/kit.cjs /absolute/path/to/ns2jb-rpc/runs/switch2-RUNID. Begin with listing, then backup, then verification. Keep original backups outside the tool folder.
Restore deliberately
Follow the bundled docs/RESTORE.md and write allowlist requirements. Restore/replace/delete alter saves. The Artemis launcher is separate from general save backup and has its own documented limits.

projects.title: OunceCake
projects.summary: Dump unencrypted romFS game assets and exeFS executable files from your own Switch 2 games, updates and DLC, including digital games, cards and Switch 2 Editions.
projects.requirements: The RPC-capable ns2jb fork linked in OunceCake’s README, an active run folder, Node.js, console LAN address and an FTP client.
projects.setup: Follow the project’s RPC setup, then run node ouncecake.cjs <path-to-ns2jb-run> and select your game. When FTP is ready, connect to the console on port 2121 using Binary/Image (TYPE I) transfer mode. The console loads the files before extraction; no system keys or independent decryption are supplied. Use your own games and keep extracted files private.
projects.status: Pinned complete script/source ZIP with bundled FTP engine. Requires the separately labelled RPC fork; Node.js22+.
guideSteps: Extract the complete package
Keep ouncecake.cjs, package.json and engine together. The ZIP includes the native FTP helper; no build step is needed for the bundled helper. Install Node.js22+ and an FTP client.
Start the required RPC host
Use the separate kurumuz RPC fork download and its README. Start node run.cjs --rpc <computer-LAN-IP>, complete the console handshake and keep the live host open.
Select the title
In the OunceCake folder run node ouncecake.cjs /absolute/path/to/ns2jb-rpc/runs/switch2-RUNID. Select your own game, update or DLC and wait for the FTP-ready message.
Copy the dump

Connect the FTP client to the Switch2LAN address on port2121, with Binary/Image(TYPE I) transfer mode. No username/password is required by this server. Copy romFS assets and exeFS files to a new computer folder with enough free space.
Close the session
Complete transfers before stopping the RPC host. Preserve your private dumps separately from these software packages; no games, keys or commercial assets are included.
